angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 11,612,787 km at 7572.22 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 0.1321 +/- 0.0172 mas (same row, RUWE 1.02): 7572.22 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 16.692 (15.328 to 18.632) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 11,612,787 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 2.903 (2.860 to 3.702) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5014 +/- 4.4 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 685473211325180928: teff_gspphot 5013.741 K (16th-84th percentiles 5009.2627-5018.084), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 685473211325180928: teff_gspphot 5013.741 K (16th-84th percentiles 5009.2627-5018.084), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gaia-dr3-685473211325180928.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.456, rounded to two decimals
